title: Count Pairs With Bitwise AND Greater Than XOR
description: Given an array `nums` of positive integers, return the number of index pairs `(i, j)` with `0 <= i < j < nums.length` such that `(nums[i] & nums[j]) > (nums[i] ^ nums[j])`.
hints: Compare `(a & b)` and `(a ^ b)` at the highest set bit of `max(a, b)`: if `a` and `b` share the same most significant `1` bit, that bit is `1` in `a & b` and `0` in `a ^ b`, guaranteeing `(a & b) > (a ^ b)`.

Conversely, if their highest set bits differ, the highest bit is `0` in `a & b` and `1` in `a ^ b`, so `(a & b) < (a ^ b)`. Bucket elements by their highest set bit position `b` and sum `c * (c - 1) / 2`.

examples.explanation: Only 4 (100) and 7 (111) share the same highest set bit (bit 2), giving 4 & 7 = 4 > 4 ^ 7 = 3.
All three 1s share highest set bit 0, forming 3 * 2 / 2 = 3 valid pairs.
1, 2, 4, 8 have distinct highest set bits (0, 1, 2, 3), so 0 pairs satisfy the condition.
